```{r}
#load packages
library(tidyverse)

#load data
train <- read_csv("data-train.csv")

#transform data
#making new variables for our summary stats

#mean = R_moment_1, C_moment_2 is variance, everything else is as commented
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    m1 = R_moment_1, m2 = R_moment_2, m3 = R_moment_3, m4 = R_moment_4,
    
    # central moments
    C_moment_2 = m2 - m1^2,                               # variance
    C_moment_3 = m3 - 3*m1*m2 + 2*m1^3,
    C_moment_4 = m4 - 4*m1*m3 + 6*m1^2*m2 - 3*m1^4,
    
    # standardized versions
    sd_R     = sqrt(C_moment_2),
    skewness = C_moment_3 / sd_R^3,
    kurtosis = C_moment_4 / sd_R^4,                       # raw kurtosis
    ex_kurt  = kurtosis - 3                               # excess kurtosis
  )

train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    Re_group = factor(Re),
    Fr_group = factor(Fr)
  )

outcomes <- c("m1", "sd_R", "skewness", "kurtosis")

summary(train[outcomes])
```

```{r}
eda_data <- train %>%
  select(St, Re_group, Fr_group, all_of(outcomes)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(outcomes),
    names_to = "outcome",
    values_to = "value"
  )

# Distributions of the outcomes
ggplot(eda_data, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, color = "white", fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal()

# Relationships with St, separated by Re and Fr
ggplot(
  eda_data,
  aes(x = St, y = value, color = Re_group)
) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(outcome ~ Fr_group, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(color = "Re", y = "Outcome", title = "Outcomes versus St by Re and Fr") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
results <- list()
fits <- list()

for (outcome in outcomes) {
  for (degree in 1:5) {
    
    model_formula <- as.formula(
      paste0(
        outcome,
        " ~ Re_group + Fr_group + poly(St, ",
        degree, ")"
      )
    )
    
    predictions <- numeric(nrow(train))
    
    # Leave-one-out cross-validation
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(train))) {
      fit <- lm(model_formula, data = train[-i, ])
      
      predictions[i] <- predict(
        fit,
        newdata = train[i, , drop = FALSE]
      )
    }
    
    observed <- train[[outcome]]
    model_name <- paste(outcome, degree, sep = "_degree_")
    
    results[[model_name]] <- data.frame(
      outcome = outcome,
      degree = degree,
      RMSE = sqrt(mean((observed - predictions)^2)),
      MAE = mean(abs(observed - predictions))
    )
    
    # Save the model fitted on all observations
    fits[[model_name]] <- lm(model_formula, data = train)
  }
}

cv_results <- do.call(rbind, results)
rownames(cv_results) <- NULL

cv_results <- cv_results[
  order(cv_results$outcome, cv_results$RMSE),
]

print(cv_results)
```

```{r}
# Plot both error measures
cv_results %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(RMSE, MAE),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "error"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = degree, y = error)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(vars(outcome, metric), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:5) +
  theme_minimal()

# Lowest LOOCV RMSE for each outcome
best_models <- cv_results %>%
  group_by(outcome) %>%
  slice_min(RMSE, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

best_models
```

## Linear Model Mean

```{r}
data <- train %>%
  mutate(
    Re = factor(Re),
    Fr = factor(Fr)
  )

train |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = St, y = m1, color = as.factor(Re), shape = as.factor(Fr))) +
  geom_point()

formulas <- list(
  no_logs  = m1 ~ St + Re + Fr,
  log_mean = log(m1) ~ St + Re + Fr,
  log_St   = m1 ~ log(St) + Re + Fr,
  log_both = log(m1) ~ log(St) + Re + Fr
)

results <- list()
mean_fits <- list()

for (model_name in names(formulas)) {
  
  predictions <- numeric(nrow(data))
  log_response <- model_name %in% c("log_mean", "log_both")
  
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(data))) {
    
    # Fit without observation i
    fit <- lm(formulas[[model_name]], data = data[-i, ])
    
    pred <- predict(fit, newdata = data[i, , drop = FALSE])
    
    if (log_response) {
      # estimated only from this fold's training observations
      correction <- mean(exp(residuals(fit)))
      pred <- exp(pred) * correction
    }
    
    predictions[i] <- pred
  }
  
  results[[model_name]] <- tibble(
    model = model_name,
    RMSE = sqrt(mean((data$m1 - predictions)^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(data$m1 - predictions))
  )
  
  mean_fits[[model_name]] <- lm(
    formulas[[model_name]],
    data = data
  )
}

mean_comparison <- bind_rows(results) %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

mean_comparison
```

Among the additive models, logging both mean volume and `St` produced the lowest original-scale LOOCV RMSE (0.01078) and MAE (0.00572). We therefore used both log transformations when investigating interactions.

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(mean_fits[["log_both"]])
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

The log–log model’s residuals were broadly centered around zero, with no strong overall curvature. The Q–Q plot appeared approximately linear, although some tail departures remain. Differences in residual spread across fitted values suggest that the transformation did not fully stabilize variance, motivating further investigation of interaction effects.

```{r}
# Compare interaction effects, keeping both log transformations
formulas <- list(
  additive = log(m1) ~ log(St) + Re + Fr,
  Re_Fr = log(m1) ~ log(St) + Re * Fr,
  St_Re = log(m1) ~ log(St) * Re + Fr,
  St_Fr = log(m1) ~ log(St) * Fr + Re,
  pairwise = log(m1) ~ (log(St) + Re + Fr)^2,
  threeway = log(m1) ~ log(St) * Re * Fr
)

interaction_results <- list()
interaction_fits <- list()

for (model_name in names(formulas)) {
  
  predictions <- numeric(nrow(data))
  
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(data))) {
    
    fit <- lm(formulas[[model_name]], data = data[-i, ])
    
    pred <- predict(fit, newdata = data[i, , drop = FALSE])
    
    # Back-transform using a training-fold smearing correction
    correction <- mean(exp(residuals(fit)))
    predictions[i] <- exp(pred) * correction
  }
  
  interaction_results[[model_name]] <- tibble(
    model = model_name,
    RMSE = sqrt(mean((data$m1 - predictions)^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(data$m1 - predictions))
  )
  
  interaction_fits[[model_name]] <- lm(
    formulas[[model_name]],
    data = data
  )
}

# Retrieve the saved models
m_additive <- interaction_fits[["additive"]]
m_Re_Fr <- interaction_fits[["Re_Fr"]]
m_St_Re <- interaction_fits[["St_Re"]]
m_St_Fr <- interaction_fits[["St_Fr"]]
m_pairwise <- interaction_fits[["pairwise"]]
m_threeway <- interaction_fits[["threeway"]]

# Compare nested models using partial F-tests
anova(m_additive, m_pairwise, m_threeway)

# Compare all candidates: lower AIC/BIC is preferred
AIC(m_additive, m_Re_Fr, m_St_Re, m_St_Fr,
    m_pairwise, m_threeway)

BIC(m_additive, m_Re_Fr, m_St_Re, m_St_Fr,
    m_pairwise, m_threeway)

# Coefficients and model summaries
summary(m_additive)
summary(m_Re_Fr)
summary(m_St_Re)
summary(m_St_Fr)
summary(m_pairwise)
summary(m_threeway)

interaction_comparison <- bind_rows(interaction_results) %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

interaction_comparison

final_mean <- m_pairwise

summary(final_mean)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(final_mean)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

The pairwise interaction model achieved the lowest original-scale LOOCV RMSE (0.00766), while the three-way model achieved the lowest MAE (0.00304). AIC favored the three-way model, whereas BIC differed by only 0.35 between the two models, offering little distinction. The nested-model ANOVA also supported adding three-way terms (p=0.0097), although this measures improvement in training fit rather than predictive performance. We selected the pairwise model because it had lower cross-validated RMSE and fewer parameters, while acknowledging that the three-way model performed better under MAE.

```{r}
fit <- final_mean

influence_table <- tibble(
  row = rownames(model.frame(fit)),
  cooks_distance = cooks.distance(fit),
  leverage = hatvalues(fit),
  studentized_residual = rstudent(fit)
) %>%
  arrange(desc(cooks_distance))

head(influence_table, 10)

# Screening threshold, not an automatic deletion rule
4 / nobs(fit)
```

```{r}
# Inspect the three observations using their row names
data[match(c("51", "8", "50"), rownames(data)),
     c("St", "Re", "Fr", "m1")]

mean_formula <- formula(final_mean)
fit_no51 <- lm(mean_formula, data = data[-51, ])
fit_no8  <- lm(mean_formula, data = data[-8, ])
fit_no50 <- lm(mean_formula, data = data[-50, ])

# Match coefficients by name
terms <- names(coef(final_mean))

coef_comparison <- cbind(
  full = coef(final_mean)[terms],
  without_51 = coef(fit_no51)[terms],
  without_8 = coef(fit_no8)[terms],
  without_50 = coef(fit_no50)[terms]
)

round(coef_comparison, 4)

# Calculate changes relative to full-model standard errors
full_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(final_mean)))[terms]

changes <- sweep(
  coef_comparison[, -1, drop = FALSE],
  1, coef(final_mean)[terms], "-"
)

changes_in_se <- sweep(changes, 1, full_se, "/")

round(changes_in_se, 2)
```

Observations 51, 8, and 50 were investigated because of their relatively large Cook’s distances and studentized residuals. Removing each observation separately produced mostly modest coefficient changes. Observation 51 had the greatest effect, shifting the `FrInf` coefficient by approximately 1.2 full-model standard errors; all other changes were less than one standard error. These checks suggested some sensitivity in individual effects but did not indicate that one observation dominated the coefficient estimates. All observations were retained because no data error or substantive reason for exclusion was identified.

```{r}
table(data$Re, data$Fr)

# Any NA coefficients are not independently estimable
coef(final_mean)

# Shows dependencies among model coefficients
alias(final_mean)
```

The interaction for `Re = 398` and `Fr = 0.3` was not estimatable because no training simulations were available at that combination.

baseline_numeric <- lm(
  log_mean ~ log_St + log_Re + logistic_Fr,
  data = data_numeric
)

summary(baseline_numeric)

plot(baseline_numeric)

```{r}
# Use the original positive outcome for Box–Cox
bc_baseline <- lm(
  m1 ~ log_St + log_Re + logistic_Fr,
  data = data_numeric
)

bc <- MASS::boxcox(
  bc_baseline,
  lambda = seq(-2, 2, by = 0.1)
)

best_lambda <- bc$x[which.max(bc$y)]
best_lambda
```

Although the Box–Cox confidence interval excluded zero, the estimated λ of approximately −0.0202 was close to zero. We therefore retained the log transformation for its simplicity and interpretable coefficients, while recognizing that Box–Cox provided a slightly better fit under the baseline model.

```{r}
numeric_formulas <- list(
  additive = log_mean ~ log_St + log_Re + logistic_Fr,
  
  Re_Fr = log_mean ~ log_St + log_Re * logistic_Fr,
  
  St_Fr = log_mean ~ log_Re + log_St * logistic_Fr,
  
  St_Re = log_mean ~ logistic_Fr + log_St * log_Re,
  
  pairwise = log_mean ~ (log_St + log_Re + logistic_Fr)^2,
  
  threeway = log_mean ~ log_St * log_Re * logistic_Fr
)
```

```{r}
numeric_results <- list()
numeric_fits <- list()

for (model_name in names(numeric_formulas)) {
  
  predictions <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data_numeric))
  
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(data_numeric))) {
    
    fit <- lm(
      numeric_formulas[[model_name]],
      data = data_numeric[-i, ]
    )
    
    pred_log <- predict(
      fit,
      newdata = data_numeric[i, , drop = FALSE]
    )
    
    # Back-transform using this training fold's residuals
    correction <- mean(exp(residuals(fit)))
    predictions[i] <- exp(pred_log) * correction
  }
  
  numeric_results[[model_name]] <- tibble(
    model = model_name,
    RMSE = sqrt(mean((data_numeric$m1 - predictions)^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(data_numeric$m1 - predictions))
  )
  
  numeric_fits[[model_name]] <- lm(
    numeric_formulas[[model_name]],
    data = data_numeric
  )
}

numeric_comparison <- bind_rows(numeric_results) %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

numeric_comparison
```

```{r}
library(glmnet)

# Candidate terms for lasso
lasso_formula <- ~ log_St * log_Re * logistic_Fr +
  I(log_St^2) + I(log_Re^2) + I(logistic_Fr^2)

# Same predictor columns for every fold
x <- model.matrix(
  lasso_formula,
  data = data_numeric
)[, -1, drop = FALSE]

y <- data_numeric$log_mean

lasso_predictions <- numeric(nrow(data_numeric))

# Choose one penalty rule before running
penalty_rule <- "lambda.1se"  # Or "lambda.min"

set.seed(2026)

# Outer LOOCV: hold out one observation
for (i in seq_len(nrow(data_numeric))) {
  
  x_train <- x[-i, , drop = FALSE]
  y_train <- y[-i]
  x_test  <- x[i, , drop = FALSE]
  
  # Inner 10-fold CV: choose the lasso penalty
  fold_id <- sample(
    rep(1:10, length.out = length(y_train))
  )
  
  fit <- cv.glmnet(
    x = x_train,
    y = y_train,
    alpha = 1,
    foldid = fold_id,
    standardize = TRUE
  )
  
  # Predict the held-out observation on the log scale
  pred_log <- as.numeric(
    predict(fit, newx = x_test, s = penalty_rule)
  )
  
  # Training residuals for the back-transformation correction
  fitted_log <- as.numeric(
    predict(fit, newx = x_train, s = penalty_rule)
  )
  
  correction <- mean(exp(y_train - fitted_log))
  
  lasso_predictions[i] <- exp(pred_log) * correction
}

# Original-scale errors, matching your ordinary regressions
lasso_results <- tibble(
  model = paste0("lasso_", penalty_rule),
  RMSE = sqrt(mean((data_numeric$m1 - lasso_predictions)^2)),
  MAE = mean(abs(data_numeric$m1 - lasso_predictions))
)

# Compare with your existing models
all_comparison <- bind_rows(
  numeric_comparison,
  lasso_results
) %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

all_comparison
```

```{r}
library(glmnet)

# Candidate predictors: main effects, two-way interactions,and quadratic terms to allow curvature
x <- model.matrix(
  ~ log_St * log_Re * logistic_Fr +
    I(log_St^2) + I(log_Re^2) + I(logistic_Fr^2),
  data = data_numeric
)[, -1]

y <- data_numeric$log_mean

# Choose the penalty using 10-fold cross-validation
set.seed(2026)

lasso_cv <- cv.glmnet(
  x = x,
  y = y,
  alpha = 1,             # Lasso
  nfolds = 10,
  standardize = TRUE
)

plot(lasso_cv)

# Coefficients at the penalty with lowest CV error
coef(lasso_cv, s = "lambda.min")

# More strongly penalized, usually simpler alternative
coef(lasso_cv, s = "lambda.1se")
```

```{r}
candidate_mean <- numeric_fits[["Re_Fr"]]

summary(candidate_mean)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(candidate_mean)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r}
# Rank observations by influence
influence_table <- tibble(
  row = rownames(model.frame(candidate_mean)),
  cooks_distance = cooks.distance(candidate_mean),
  leverage = hatvalues(candidate_mean),
  studentized_residual = rstudent(candidate_mean)
) %>%
  arrange(desc(cooks_distance))

head(influence_table, 10)

# Screening threshold—not an automatic deletion rule
4 / nobs(candidate_mean)
```

```{r}
# Observations above the screening threshold
flagged_rows <- influence_table %>%
  filter(cooks_distance > 4 / nobs(candidate_mean)) %>%
  pull(row)

# Inspect their original values
data_numeric[
  match(flagged_rows, rownames(data_numeric)),
  c("St", "Re", "Fr", "m1")
]

# Refit the same model, omitting one flagged observation at a time
sensitivity_fits <- setNames(
  lapply(flagged_rows, function(id) {
    reduced_data <- data_numeric[
      rownames(data_numeric) != id, ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
    
    lm(formula(candidate_mean), data = reduced_data)
  }),
  paste0("without_", flagged_rows)
)

# Coefficient changes measured in full-model standard errors
full_coef <- coef(candidate_mean)
full_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(candidate_mean)))

changes_in_se <- sapply(sensitivity_fits, function(fit) {
  (coef(fit)[names(full_coef)] - full_coef) / full_se
})

round(changes_in_se, 2)
```

Nine observations exceeded the Cook’s distance screening threshold. Removing each individually changed all coefficients by less than 0.62 full-model standard errors, suggesting that the coefficient estimates were reasonably robust to individual influential observations.

```{r}
summary(candidate_mean)
confint(candidate_mean)
```

Mean cluster volume increased with St, with doubling St associated with approximately 14.6% higher fitted volume, holding Re and Fr fixed. Higher Re was associated with lower volume across the observed gravity settings. The positive Re–Fr interaction indicated that this relationship became less negative as Fr increased.
